title: P-256 paired stored-leaf birthday search with exact scalar kernels

claims.statement: For the exact protected full-production P-256 target Q=[x]P, the cold classical paired stored-leaf algorithm in proof.md returns the canonical scalar x with probability at least 0.39 over uniform challenges and fresh independent coins, under the explicitly supplied scalar-instruction machine and ideal-coin conventions. Its total work is at most 2^126.62 target-operation units at C=1000, including preprocessing, capped failures, all routing and coordination, resolution, verification and output. Peak memory is below 2^136 bytes, preprocessing below 2^118 units and included, and nonuniform advice is zero. The construction uses the order-two negation quotient only, q1=188761551, q2=2^27, 2^72 nodes, exact canonical Montgomery P-256 arithmetic, and paired X+Y/X-Y outputs from one batch inverse. The rational collision/cap bound exceeds 0.3901; no random-walk or NFS smoothness hypothesis is used. This is an analytical computation claim with astronomical memory, not a production run or a physical feasibility claim. The complete field, probability, cost and memory arguments and their implementation evidence are supplied.

experiments.purpose: Run independent field and pair checks, full batch inversion, metadata and capacity controls, small complete two-hop routing, actual toy scalar recovery, and exact probability/cold-work/layout consequences. Test scope is distinguished from the production proof.
